ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Assessing fracture geometry

A 41-year-old man has a visible scaphoid waist fracture on radiographs. Before choosing treatment, the surgeon wants a clearer assessment of fragment displacement and the fracture configuration. Which additional study is particularly useful for this purpose?

  1. Bone scintigraphy
  2. Ultrasound of the flexor tendons
  3. MR angiography of the forearm arteries
  4. Repeat examination without additional imaging
  5. CT of the wrist
Answer and explanation

CT of the wrist

CT provides detailed bony assessment of fracture geometry and displacement.

Option explanations

CT of the wrist: CT provides detailed bony assessment of fracture geometry and displacement.

Bone scintigraphy: It can detect increased bone turnover but does not define fragment geometry as precisely as CT.

Ultrasound of the flexor tendons: This is not the best study of scaphoid fracture displacement.

MR angiography of the forearm arteries: Large-vessel imaging does not answer the question of fracture geometry.

Repeat examination without additional imaging: Examination alone cannot quantify the fracture displacement.
